This edition record identifies the Latin normative text, not any vernacular Lectionary approved for a territory.

passages.context: The Advent weekday block of the Proper of Time, marginal nn. 175-201. What is established here is the block's own arrangement, not any of its words. Its first three series of weekdays are headed by the week of Advent and by the weekday within that week: the first week opens at n. 175 with its Monday, the second at n. 181, and the third at n. 187. The third series prints five weekdays and no Saturday, closing at n. 191 with its Friday. An acclamation formulary appointed for those weekdays follows at n. 192, headed for the weekdays of Advent as far as 16 December. Eight further weekdays are then headed by their civil date, nn. 193-200, under a section heading naming the band 17 to 24 December and carrying a rubric on days displaced by an occurring Sunday; n. 193 is 17 December, n. 194 is 18 December and n. 195 is 19 December. A second acclamation formulary, headed for the weekdays of Advent from 17 to 24 December, closes the block at n. 201. The 16 December boundary and the change of key grammar at 17 December are therefore the book's own, printed in its headings, and not an inference from the Universal Norms.

passages.context: The Ordinary Time weekday block of the Proper of Time, marginal nn. 305-509, the longest single run in the book. What is established here is the block's own arrangement, not any of its words. Its series are headed by the week of Ordinary Time and by the weekday within that week, and each numbered day is set in two parallel columns headed as the first and the second year, so that the first reading and the responsorial psalm differ between the two while the acclamation and the Gospel are printed once across both. This two-column setting is the printed form of the two-year ferial course, and it is confined to this block: no other weekday run in the book is set this way. The block opens at n. 305 with the Monday of the first week and closes its numbered weekdays at n. 508 with the Saturday of the thirty-fourth week; n. 305 carries beneath it a rubric on the years in which the Baptism of the Lord falls on the Monday of the first week of Ordinary Time. A single acclamation formulary for these weekdays follows at n. 509, and it carries within itself a short supplementary set for the last week and a pointer to a formulary printed earlier in the book; the numbered weekday sequence of the Proper of Time ends there.

passages.context: The Lenten weekday block of the Proper of Time, marginal nn. 219-256. What is established here is the block's own arrangement, not any of its words. passages.context: The Christmas Time weekday block of the Proper of Time, marginal nn. 202-218. What is established here is the block's own arrangement, not any of its words. Every series in it is keyed by civil date, and the season's weekdays fall into five runs. Three days are headed both by their civil date, 29, 30 and 31 December, and by their place within the octave of the Nativity, nn. 202-204. Four more are headed by civil date alone, 2 to 5 January, nn. 205-208. Two are headed by civil date, 6 and 7 January, nn. 209-210, each carrying its own rubric restricting it to regions in which the Epiphany is kept on the Sunday falling on 7 or 8 January. An acclamation formulary for the season before the Epiphany stands at n. 211. Six further series are headed both by the civil dates 7 to 12 January and as the weekdays after the Epiphany, nn. 212-217, opening under two rubrics registered separately at the passage for n. 212. A second acclamation formulary, for the weekdays after the Epiphany, closes the block at n. 218. The acclamation formularies therefore divide the season at the Epiphany in the same way the day series do.

passages.context: Marginal n. 205 of the Christmas Time weekday block, the weekday headed by the civil date 2 January, on printed page 118. It is registered on its own because of the rubric printed beneath its four Lectionary slots, which is one of the two rubrics by which the Order of Readings disposes of the Christmas Time weekdays where the Epiphany has been transferred. In substance, and without reproducing its wording: in regions where the Epiphany is celebrated on the Sunday falling between 2 and 8 January, the readings proposed for the days 7 to 12 January are taken after the Epiphany, and the date-headed days that would otherwise have followed n. 205 are omitted. The rubric is therefore the book's own answer to a question the Universal Norms leave to the competent authority, and it is an answer about the Order of Readings alone: it says nothing about how the Missal heads or appoints these days, and no witness of the Missal's Proper of Time is held here. The companion rubric stands at n. 212 and is registered separately.

passages.context: Marginal n. 212 of the Christmas Time weekday block, on printed page 121, the first of the six series headed both by a civil date, 7 January, and as the weekday after the Epiphany. It is registered on its own because of the two rubrics printed above it at the head of that run, which together are the companion to the rubric at n. 205 and the second half of the Order of Readings' disposition of these weekdays where the Epiphany has been transferred. In substance, and without reproducing their wording: the first directs that the readings assigned to the days 7 to 12 January serve the days following the solemnity of the Epiphany even where that solemnity has been placed on a Sunday, as far as the Saturday following; the second directs that from the Monday after the Sunday on which the Baptism of the Lord is celebrated, that is the Sunday occurring after 6 January, the readings of Ordinary Time begin, whatever remains of the 7 to 12 January run being omitted. The run these rubrics head therefore hangs from the Epiphany rather than from the calendar, and its length is not fixed. This establishes the arrangement of the Order of Readings and nothing about the Missal's Proper of Time, which is held in no witness here.

passages.context: Praenotanda n. 104 with its footnotes 115 and 116, on printed p. XLIV. Subdivision 1 governs Week I and the Monday Baptism case, subdivision 2 the consecutive Sunday numbering and the suspension of the readings of the week in which Ash Wednesday occurs, and subdivision 3 the resumption after Pentecost, including the omission of the first week that would have been taken after Pentecost when there are thirty-three Sundays. Footnote 115 works the thirty-four-week case with six weeks before Lent and notes that Trinity Sunday takes the place of an Ordinary Time Sunday; footnote 116 works the thirty-three-week case with five weeks before Lent, omitting the sixth week and beginning from the seventh.

work.description: The postconciliar Roman Rite book of readings for Mass, first published in 1969 and issued in a second Latin typical edition in 1981, distinct from the Missal in which the prayers and antiphons are printed. Its Praenotanda state the principles governing the selection and arrangement of the readings, including the three-year Sunday cycle, the two-year weekday first-reading cycle, and the criteria of length, difficulty and omission.
work.title: Ordo lectionum Missae
